result:
The last streetlamp on the block has been flickering for three nights. Not the ordinary, tired stutter of a bulb about to die, but a deliberate pulse—three short, three long, three short—as if the light itself has remembered Morse code and is trying to say something to the empty sidewalk. 

I stood under it tonight with my hands in my pockets, counting. The pattern held. A woman walking a small dog paused a few meters away, watched me watching the lamp, then shrugged and moved on. The dog glanced back once, ears pricked, as though it too had noticed the rhythm and decided it was none of its business.

When the light finally steadied, the ordinary yellow returning, I felt oddly disappointed. I had been ready to answer. I still don’t know what I would have said. 

Some signals are only meant to be received, not returned. The lamp knows this. So does the dog. I’m still learning.
